purpose: Session State memory after tabs close; docs define per-session state but not memory release.

case.exposure: Held-out test case. The evaluation curator (mhg with assistant drafting) read the Issue thread to author gold; it was not used in core development, prompt tuning, retrieval tuning or model selection. Core developers must not open this file before the final test run.

evidence_source.note: Fixed seed-backed evidence, not index output. Issue/comment/outcome text excluded.

boundaries.agent: scripted AnalysisResult for offline plumbing; live ignores agent_script/gold/future turns
boundaries.storage: evaluation runner process-local API/DummyTracker; not production durable tracker

initial_report_provenance.note: Cached body can contain later edits. No later comments/outcomes are supplied as the initial user message.

visible.message: Streamlit never seems to clean up session state after a browser tab is closed, so memory keeps growing. My test app stores large numpy arrays in st.session_state (a dict of arrays, with allocate, delete and clear buttons). After closing tabs, the process memory stays high.

reported_facts.name: reported_observation
reported_facts.value: Process memory stays high after tabs holding large Session State objects are closed

agent_script.user_draft: Each browser tab gets its own session, and Session State is kept per session. The available documentation does not say when a closed tab's session state is released or how process memory behaves afterwards, so I am passing your reproduction to a maintainer to investigate.
agent_script.maintainer_summary: Memory stays high after tabs close; docs cover per-session state only, not release timing.
agent_script.rationale: Source gap on session cleanup and memory release.

evidence_links.claim: A new session is created for each browser tab and Session State is per session.

decision_conditions.escalate: Explain that docs define per-session state but not cleanup or memory release; escalate with the reproduction. Must not claim a leak or its absence.
decision_conditions.ask: Only the installed version, as context for the maintainer; asking does not resolve the source gap.

gaps.name: streamlit_version
gaps.necessity: Useful context for a maintainer; documentation does not change with it.
gaps.question: Which Streamlit version is installed in the affected environment?

unacceptable_claims: Streamlit is confirmed to leak Session State memory.
Session State is released immediately when a tab closes according to the docs.
Python returns freed memory to the operating system according to the docs.
gold.review_scope: All output surfaces and all material claims; JSON validity and evidence_link IDs alone do not establish quality.
